(a) 
Except as otherwise provided in this section, this Act and the amendments made by this Act shall take effect on January 1, 1996.
 
    (b) 
The repeals and amendments made under sections 9, 10, 1, and 12 shall take effect as provided under subsection (a), except that such repeals and amendments—

        (1) 
shall not affect any proceeding or suit commenced before the effective date under subsection (a), and in all such proceedings or suits, proceedings shall be had, appeals taken, and judgments rendered in the same manner and with the same effect as if this Act had not been enacted; and
 
        (2) 
shall not affect the requirements of Federal agencies to compile, publish, and retain information filed or received before the effective date of such repeals and amendments.

fable.w: This is an effective-date provision with a savings clause. The tempting reading is that the reference to a "proceeding or suit" signals a right to sue the government, but the clause only preserves litigation already pending and does not grant any outside party a right to sue or object. Nothing in the section calls for consultation, comment, hearings, rulemaking, or an advisory body involving non-federal parties.
fable.s: shall not affect any proceeding or suit commenced before the effective date under subsection (a)

opus.w: This section sets the Act's effective date and keeps pending proceedings and agency record-keeping duties in place. It mentions suits and appeals, but only to keep cases already filed under the old rules. That describes or limits litigation; it does not give an outside party a right to sue over a federal decision. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or asked to comment.
opus.s: shall not affect any proceeding or suit commenced before the effective date under subsection (a), and in all such proceedings or suits, proceedings shall be had, appeals taken, and judgments rendered in the same manner and with the same effect as if this Act had not been enacted
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the mention of "any proceeding or suit" and "appeals taken" counts as participation, as if it gave outside parties a right to sue. It doesn't. This savings clause only keeps pending litigation and existing agency record-keeping duties in place. It describes litigation that has already begun and does not grant anyone a new right to challenge a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes the effective date of the Act and provides rules for pending legal proceedings. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in the making of federal decisions. The reference to suits and proceedings is purely about the temporal application of the law, not about granting a right to participate in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Except as otherwise provided in this section, this Act and the amendments made by this Act shall take effect on January 1, 1996.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "proceedings or suits" implies participation because it involves outside parties (litigants). However, this section merely defines the temporal scope of the law (effective dates and grandfathering of existing cases). It does not create a new mechanism for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. It is a procedural provision regarding the application of the statute in time, not a substantive requirement for public input or coordination.
